questions.prompt: For a row-major array a[y * width + x], which index should come from threadIdx.x?
questions.explanation: x varies fastest in memory, so consecutive lanes should differ in x.

questions.prompt: Structs of 3 floats (12 bytes) in AoS layout. A warp reads field 0 of 32 consecutive structs. What's the efficiency, in percent? (One decimal place.)
questions.explanation: The span is 32 × 12 = 384 bytes, 12 sectors, for 128 useful bytes: 33.3%.

questions.prompt: Why is AoS natural on CPUs but SoA on GPUs?
options: A CPU thread uses all fields of one object (one cache line); a GPU instruction uses one field of 32 objects
questions.explanation: The unit of access differs: one object per thread versus one field across a warp.

questions.prompt: Blocks of 8×32 (x by y) process a row-major image. What's wrong?
options: Each warp covers 8 consecutive x values on 4 rows, so it touches 4 separate 32-byte runs instead of one 128-byte run
questions.explanation: Narrow blocks make warps span several rows. Use at least 32 threads in x.

questions.prompt: Rows of a float image are 1,000 elements (4,000 bytes) long. Why might you pad each row to 1,024 elements?
options: So every row starts on a 128-byte boundary, avoiding an extra straddled sector per warp
Because widths must be powers of two
questions.explanation: Pitched allocation keeps rows aligned; that's what cudaMallocPitch does.

questions.prompt: Which patterns cannot be fully coalesced by changing indexing alone?
options: Reading interleaved 3-byte RGB pixels one per thread
A grid-stride loop over an array
questions.explanation: Both need threads to cooperate through shared memory. Grid-stride loops and vector add are already ideal.
